fable.w: The tempting reading is that the 'regular notification procedures' are a form of consultation, but the notification goes to the congressional Committees on Appropriations, which are inside the federal government. The rest of the section only earmarks Foreign Military Financing funds for named countries. No public comment, rulemaking, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue is provided.
fable.s: Provided, That such funds shall only be made available subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.

opus.w: This section sets aside Foreign Military Financing funds for specific countries. Its only procedural requirement is notice to the congressional Appropriations Committees, and Congress is inside the federal government, so that notice is not participation. The countries are aid recipients rather than consultees, and the 2003 Joint Defense Assessment is a past document. The section has no comment period, hearing, outside advisory body, or right to sue.
opus.s: Provided, That such funds shall only be made available subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that "the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations" is a procedural step before funds are released, so it must count as participation. It doesn't. Those committees are part of Congress, which is inside the federal government. The foreign countries named only receive aid; they have no say in the decision. The "Joint Defense Assessment of 2003" is a past document, not a future process that brings in outsiders.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires notification to the Committees on Appropriations. Under the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Therefore, this is intra-governmental coordination/notification, not participation with outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: Provided, That such funds shall only be made available subject to the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations" constitutes participation because it involves informing an external body. However, Congress and its committees are explicitly defined as being INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, notifications to Congress are intra-governmental communications and do not count as participation with outside parties.
